title: Grace-period Scaled Throttler with Tiered Degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Design and implement a graceful, per-fleet admission controller that provides short-duration throughput guarantees via a configurable grace period, while enabling progressive degradation tiers (soft throttle -> demotion -> shed) for overloaded dedicated pools. The goal is to give small bursts predictable completion while protecting long-running tenant guarantees and SLOs. Key capabilities:
- Grace window: allow transient bursts above steady quotas for a short window with token accounting; revert to steady-state afterwards.
- Scaled throttling curve: slowly reduce allowed concurrency over a configurable time horizon instead of immediate hard caps.
- Tenant-aware demotion: redirect excess requests to lower-cost model variants or degraded mode with structured response indicating fallbacks.
- Coordinated autoscaler signals: expose per-fleet headroom metric and a proactive shed recommendation that informs the autoscaler to bring up capacity before hard SLO drops occur.
- Observability hooks: per-request admission decisions, grace consumption metrics, demotion counts, and time-in-degradation histograms for console dashboards and alerts.
Acceptance criteria:
1) Unit + integration tests for grace window accounting and scaled-throttling behavior.
2) Bench harness demonstrates burst completion rate improves by >=30% for sub-second bursts without increasing median P95 latency for steady traffic.
3) Console dashboard surfaces grace utilization and demotion events; ops runbook updated.
4) Feature gate and rollout plan for dedicated fleets; can be disabled per-customer.

2026-02-18 - Samir Patel: Implemented local sim harness; observed graceful window prevents 80% of burst shed events in synthetic load. Pushed prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5821
2026-02-25 - Design Review (Priya Rao): UI needs to show both grace utilization and projected time to refill tokens. Added dashboard mockups in Figma (link: https://www.figma.com/file/GraceThrottle).
2026-03-02 - Security (Ben Liu): Reviewed threat model; KMS not required, but ensure demotion responses do not leak tenant metadata. No blocking issues.

2026-03-08 - Samir Patel: Integration test failing intermittently under long-tail latencies. Root cause: token refill scheduler misaligned with GC pauses. Added jitter and resilient timers; tests stabilizing.
2026-03-14 - Ava Martinez: Roadmap sync decided phased rollout: internal canary -> pilot customers (2 tenants) -> general availability. Added release notes draft and canary enrollment checklist.
